items.headline: Saudi Arabia replaces commander of coalition fighting the Houthis
items.summary: A royal decree on Monday put General Fayyad al-Ruwaili in charge of the Saudi Joint Forces, replacing Lt Gen Fahd bin Hamad al-Salman, as the Houthis edge closer to Aden.

items.headline: Russian attacks kill three in Ukraine as EU accuses Moscow
items.summary: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said Vladimir Putin is making maximalist demands and stalling talks aimed at ending the war.

items.headline: UK seeks closer ties with the EU
items.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham's government is pushing for a closer relationship with Brussels; UK defence shares rose on Monday on hopes of deeper UK-EU cooperation.

items.headline: FTSE 100 slips as miners and US tech weigh
items.summary: The index fell 0.2% to 10,881.55 on Monday after earlier gains, and the FTSE 250 lost 0.4% to 24,700.06, ahead of Nvidia's results and Anthropic's market debut.

items.headline: Defence firms rally while miners fall on copper prices
items.summary: Babcock and BAE Systems were the FTSE 100's top gainers on Monday, while metal miners retreated as copper prices dropped.

items.headline: Nasdaq falls more than 2% as Nvidia drags AI shares
items.summary: The US tech index fell for a third day running, with Nvidia due to report its first results since Jensen Huang's resignation.

items.headline: US to name AI 'national champions', reports say
items.summary: The Wall Street Journal says more than two dozen firms, including Nvidia, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic, would get faster export licences and federal financing help. The companies have not confirmed it.

items.headline: US moves to block China's remote access to AI chips
items.summary: Washington is acting to stop Chinese firms renting access to advanced AI chips remotely, amid the Nvidia scandal.

items.headline: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet for AI agent purchases
items.summary: The new feature is meant to let AI agents pay for things on a user's behalf.
